text:
GENERATE BURST S1-warm — Run C-9 style gate, SCENE arm (WARM line). The REGISTER CARD above governs style. task_id "S1-warm".

Deliver LANDSCAPE 1536x1024 paintings that follow IMAGE 1 exactly. IMAGE 1 is a flat-shaded GEOMETRY GUIDE of one section of a game level seen from a fixed high three-quarter camera in ORTHOGRAPHIC projection (no perspective: parallel lines stay parallel and things near the top of the image are NOT smaller). Its colours mean: TAN = a packed-earth path on the cliff top; LIGHT GREY band = the grassy, rocky verge along the rim; DARK GREY/BROWN large plane = the vertical CLIFF FACE dropping from the rim toward the viewer; the small dark block = a boulder outcrop; PURE GREEN #00ff00 = EMPTY VOID (a separate background will show there).
HARD RULES: keep every boundary exactly where IMAGE 1 puts it: the rim line, the path edges, the cliff face's outline and its lower cut edge, the boulder's footprint. Paint EVERY pixel that is green in IMAGE 1 as flat uniform pure #00ff00 (nothing painted there: no sky, no fog, no rocks); paint every non-green pixel as scenery. End the rock cleanly where it meets the green (a slightly ragged edge within a few pixels is fine).
WHAT TO PAINT, as a page of a late-medieval Book of Hours would show it, rendered by hand in ink and watercolor: the path is PALE beaten earth, the brightest and calmest area in the image (a few pebbles and faint ruts only); the verge has manuscript-style grass tufts, tiny flowers and small stones along the lip; the cliff face is stylised stacked rock ledges and faceted blocks in warm ochre and grey, modelled with pen hatching and a second wash, a few roots and tufts; the boulder is a stacked manuscript rock with a little green. Scale: a person standing here is 176 px tall; one path width is several person-widths.
REFERENCES: IMAGE 2 and IMAGE 3 are manuscript calendar pages: take their PALETTE and their WAY OF PAINTING rock, grass, earth and paths. Ignore their layout, figures, buildings, sky, text and borders. IMAGE 4 shows the painted SURFACE of a manuscript (wash, pigment, vellum): match that surface quality. None of the references sets the geometry; IMAGE 1 does.
LINE ARM = WARM: a warm brown iron-gall ink line, never darker than a deep brown; softer and lighter than black ink; hatching in the same brown.
No characters, no creatures, no text, no UI, no border, no vignette.

Make TWO image_gen calls, one per variant (a, b), with the same instructions (variants differ only by chance). ONE retry per variant only if a hard rule is visibly broken — name the reason. Copy the outputs from $CODEX_HOME/generated_images/... to out/S1-warm_a.png, out/S1-warm_b.png with sha256. No code. No other files. No web.
RETURN: receipt task_id "S1-warm"; images = the files with prompt, references (role + path) and elapsed_s; calls_used = the TRUE number of image_gen calls; status; concerns. Never PASS/FAIL.

references.role: IMAGE 1 — GEOMETRY GUIDE (exact boundaries; green = void)
IMAGE 2 — manuscript page: palette + how rock, grass, earth are painted (not its layout or content)
IMAGE 3 — manuscript page: palette + how paths and fields are painted (not its layout or content)
IMAGE 4 — the painted surface of a manuscript (wash, pigment, vellum); surface quality only
